correctness.rationale: Reflect the two windows E_epsilon around ±a and set d=2a. The sinc Fourier concentration kernel splits unitarily into parity blocks T_eta/epsilon with rank-one limit h_eta J, h_eta=k(0)+eta k(d)>0; the top eigenvalue 2h_eta is isolated and simple for W near each W0=nπ/d. Analytic perturbation gives lambda_eta=2epsilon h_eta+(2epsilon^3/3)[k"(0)+eta k"(d)+k'(d)^2/h_eta]+O(epsilon^5). The first-order mixing contribution is required. The normalized parity gap equals k(d)+(epsilon²/3)[k"(d)-k'(d)^2 k(d)/(k(0)^2-k(d)^2)]+O(epsilon⁴). At W0, k(d)=0, ∂W k(d)=(-1)^n/π, k"(d)=-2W0(-1)^n/(πd²), so analytic IFT yields a unique local transverse crossing W_n(epsilon)=W0[1+epsilon²/(6a²)+O(epsilon⁴)]. Both sector top eigenvalues are simple and separated from the smaller spectrum, so full leading eigenvalue has multiplicity exactly two. Independent 36-node parity Nyström quadrature for a=1 and n=1,2,3, epsilon=.15 and .075 agrees with positive O(epsilon²) shift and 1/6 normalized coefficient. Numerics cannot prove all fixed n or rigorous O(epsilon⁴) remainder.
residual_risks: Analytic perturbation result is local for fixed n and small epsilon<a, not uniform as n grows.
